@graph.description: Tilt is when emotion takes over and your plan stops governing. Spot it in 10 seconds — body and behavior scan, any two signals, circuit breaker fires.
@graph.headline: Tilt in Trading: What It Is, Signs & How to Stop It

acceptedAnswer.text: Tilt is emotional decision-making after a loss or a string of losses: increasing your size to recover, abandoning your entry rules, adding to losers. The defining mark is not the emotion itself — it is that the plan has stopped governing. The market is still the market, but you are no longer you. (Practitioner definition per futureshive's FAQ, verified 2026-10-17.)

The widely cited origin is the pinball machine: a frustrated player physically tilts the machine to save the ball, the machine flashes "TILT," freezes the flippers, and the ball is lost for certain. Poker adopted the word for the frustrated, over-aggressive play that follows a bad beat; trading inherited it. The metaphor holds across all three: frustration-driven over-aggression is self-punishing — you lose the ball by trying to force it.

mainEntity.name: Where does the term "on tilt" come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Run the two-layer scan. The body (shallow rapid breathing, sweaty palms, tightened jaw or neck, racing heartbeat, feeling flushed) plus the tilt-specific behavior tells: bigger risk suddenly feeling rational, the "get it back right now" thought looping, watching the rupee P&L instead of the chart, autopilot clicks and fat-finger errors (wrong size, wrong side, missed stops), the planned window quietly reopening. Any two signals from either layer = stop for at least 30 minutes.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I'm on tilt?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — C-game is the trader; tilt is the in-session state that produces C-game behavior; revenge trading is one of the behaviors tilt wears. Tilt is the state where the plan stops governing; revenge trading is the specific post-loss form, the recovery trade driven by the feeling that the loss is a debt the market owes you. Same circuit breaker, same cure — the loss-side protocol is tilt's protocol wearing a revenge mask.

mainEntity.name: Is revenge trading the same as tilt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Catch the state first with the scan: any two signals from either layer = circuit breaker, minimum 30-minute pause. For the response, the chapters ahead already own it — the post-loss protocol lives in the revenge-trading chapter, the A+ re-entry filter in the overtrading chapter. This chapter's share is detection, and detection is where the damage stops.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop tilting after a loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two overlooked trigger classes. First, your physical state: bad sleep, poor food, alcohol, stress outside trading — all of it changes your tilt sensitivity before the first candle (one forum trader's practitioner observation). Second, market structure: a stop-out on a volatility spike can trigger a helplessness-and-adrenaline reaction that tilts a calm trader. Run the pre-session audit: rate your emotional intensity 1–10 — if you're already at 6 before the first trade, you're starting tilted, and the day starts with reduced size or not at all.
